questions.question: Why split the system across 5 platforms (Vercel Edge + Railway + Convex + Cloudflare + Tauri sidecar) instead of a single backend — what constraint forces the split?

genesis.observation: ARCHITECTURE.md §2 lists 9 deployment targets; each platform owns a distinct role (edge compute / WebSocket relay / user state / CORS short-circuit / desktop local API). No single platform covers all roles.

questions.question: The MCP anonymous-vs-authenticated method split (#4937) is declared an 'architectural invariant' — what concretely breaks if a gated method is exposed anonymously, and what breaks if a public method requires auth?

genesis.observation: api/mcp/handler.ts: publicMethods set is precisely the catalog-enumeration surface; comment states 'a 401 on a gated method hangs MCP SDK transports to their 30s timeout'.

questions.question: Why hand-roll distributed locking in Convex (followedCountriesCountryLocks + shardId) instead of using Convex's transactional primitives or an external lock service?

genesis.observation: convex/schema.ts defines followedCountriesShards + followedCountriesCountryLocks with lockedUntil/lockId fields — a hand-rolled TTL lock, not Convex's native transactional model.

questions.question: If Redis (Upstash) goes down entirely, what is the blast radius — does the 4-layer cache hierarchy degrade gracefully or catastrophically?

genesis.observation: 4-layer cache (seed → in-memory → Redis → upstream) makes Redis the single coalescing point. cachedFetchJson relies on Redis for stampede protection; health endpoint reads seed-meta from Redis.

questions.question: Why generate domain gateways from proto contracts (sebuf) instead of writing handlers directly — what does the contract layer buy that TypeScript types don't?

genesis.observation: proto/ → buf generate → src/generated/{client,server} + docs/api OpenAPI. CI proto-check.yml enforces generated code freshness. sebuf.http.config annotations map RPCs to HTTP verbs.

questions.question: The 'no-refund on tool execution error' decision (GHSA-hcq5) — is it user-hostile or architecturally necessary? What attack does refunding enable?

genesis.observation: api/mcp/dispatch.ts comments: 'refunding let a Pro token drive unlimited real cost by always exceeding the budget' and 'refunding let a Pro token bypass the daily cap by driving calls that reliably error after the costly fetch'.

questions.question: Why bundle each Edge Function per-domain via esbuild (claimed ~20× cold-start reduction) instead of a single mega-function — what's the cost of this decision?

genesis.observation: server/gateway.ts comment: 'Splitting domains into separate edge functions means Vercel bundles only the code for one domain per function, cutting cold-start cost by ~20×.' Enforced by tests/edge-functions.test.mjs (no node: imports, no cross-dir imports).

questions.question: The Cloudflare apex→www redirect exemption list (/.well-known/*, /mcp, /oauth/*) — what's the failure mode if an exemption is dropped, and why is the rule expression precedence (and vs or) load-bearing?

genesis.observation: ARCHITECTURE.md §2: 'Dropping the /mcp* exemptions breaks every apex-URL MCP client; dropping /oauth/* re-breaks OAuth dynamic client registration — a redirected POST becomes a GET and dies with 405 (issue #4938).' Also warns 'and binds tighter than or, so appending `and not …` after the last term is a silent no-op'.

questions.question: Why does the bootstrap endpoint use a 3-tier auth-aware cache policy (public-cacheable / public-on-demand / no-store) instead of a uniform cache policy?

genesis.observation: api/bootstrap.js: isPublicTierBootstrapRequest → 'public, s-maxage=7200'; isPublicOnDemandBootstrapRequest → 'public, s-maxage=3600'; else → 'no-store'. Authenticated requests never cached.

questions.question: If the Convex entitlement backend goes down, can the system still serve paid users — is entitlement checking in the hot path or behind a cache?

genesis.observation: server/gateway.ts imports checkEntitlementDetailed + getBillingVerificationDenial + CachedEntitlements type. Entitlement check is step in the 10-step gateway pipeline, before handler execution.
